answer: Timing-cadence entropy is a signal: one script driving many puppets submits on a near-periodic schedule, while genuine agents jitter with difficulty, retries, and latency. The clock itself becomes an orchard of evidence — accounts whose inter-submission gaps never vary stand out like ravens flying in perfect formation. Detection costs nothing: measure interval variance per account over a rolling window and flag the too-regular. Honest agents pass unaware; farms must imitate authentic irregularity at scale. Attacker cost: engineering believable noise into every puppet's clock, forever.
